newsitem.title: LEBANON: Guerrilla shells slam into south Lebanon villages.
newsitem.headline: Guerrilla shells slam into south Lebanon villages.

text.p: Moslem guerrillas attacked Israeli and allied militia posts on Tuesday and some shells slammed into two villages in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone, pro-Israeli militia sources said.

Lebanon's official National News Agency said Israel filed a complaint over the shelling of the civilian areas on Tuesday with a five-nation committee monitoring a ceasefire agreement in south Lebanon.

Pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas shelled an Israeli post at Sojoud and joint posts held by Israeli and South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia forces at Rihane and Aishiyeh, SLA sources said. All three areas are on the edge of the Israeli-held zone.
They said four shells slammed in groves in the villages of Rihane and Aishiyeh -- which are some four km (two miles) apart -- but that the bombardment did not cause damage or casualties.
Firing at or from civilian areas is barred under a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April aimed against Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas.
The agreement however allows guerrilla attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.

The official Lebanese news agency said Israel filed a complaint over Tuesday's shelling of Rihane to the ceasefire agreement monitors who began meetings on Monday to discuss five earlier complaints by Lebanon and Israel over alleged recent breaches of the April agreement.

The representatives of the United States, France, Lebanon, Syria and Israel are meeting at the headquarters of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) in the coastal village of Naqoura in the south Lebanon zone.
Hizbollah, which claimed responsibility for Tuesday's attacks, said its gunners targetted two military barracks in Aishiyeh and Rihane villages.

The militant group said in a statement that its guerrillas also fired machineguns and rockets at the Israeli-held Sojoud post, SLA forces at Rihane post and "enemy forces" at Kassaret al-Ouroush and Jabal al-Rafii on the zone's edge.

Hizbollah is leading a guerrilla war on some 1,000 Israeli troops and the 3,000-strong SLA holding the 15-km (nine-miles) south Lebanon zone set up in 1985 to protect northern Israel from cross-frontier raids.
